surface_mechanism_description: Atomic interdiffusions and surface evaporations occurred during the post-growth thermal annealing processes. Atomic diffusions of oxygen from the grown MoO3 towards the Si substrate lead to the formation of a thin SiOx layer at the interface between MoO3 and Si. Upon annealing at elevated temperatures, the atomic diffusions are enhanced, leading to the reactions SiOx + (2 - x)O → SiO2. Outwards diffusions of Si atoms from the Si substrate through the SiOx interlayer to form SiOx at the MoO3/SiOx interface may also occur at elevated temperatures. Both contribute to an increase in the effective thickness of the interfacial SiO2. The surface evaporation of the ALD MoO3 might be balanced by in-plane clustering due to interactions with the substrate, which in turn led to the formation of MoO3 particles.
